title: heterogeneous-quant-fallback-coordinator-and-kv-prefetch-adapter
author: Priya Shah
description:
Motivation: On mixed-precision fleets we observe sporadic tail-latency spikes when the serving runtime switches between INT8 and FP8 kernels under pressure. Root causes include coarse-grained fallback logic (per-device) and KV-cache prefetches that assume a single precision for the entire microbatch. This PR introduces two cooperating components: (1) a HeterogeneousQuantFallbackCoordinator that reasons about per-request and per-layer precision compatibility and orchestrates graceful handoffs between quantized kernels (INT8/FP8) and the full-precision path; and (2) a KVPrefetchAdapter that annotates KV prefetch windows with precision hints and aligns cache warming to the coordinator's decisions.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a coordinator service inside the runtime scheduler that keeps lightweight, epoched precision-maps for active model versions and routes requests to the most compatible kernel path while minimizing kernel switch overhead.
- KVPrefetchAdapter propagates precision hints into the KV cache warming pipeline so that prefetched KV entries use the quantization layout expected by the chosen kernel or include a small inline dequantization token when mixed precision is unavoidable.
- Introduces a small lock-free per-GPU staging structure used by the coordinator to avoid global scheduler locks during precision transitions.
- Adds metrics and tracing hooks (precision.route, precision.transition_ms, kv.prefetch_mode) so we can observe fallback frequency and prefetch mismatches.
- Includes unit tests and microbenchmarks (CPU/CUDA) and a perf harness to reproduce the tail-latency scenarios.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- The coordinator chooses per-request precision by combining: request-level hints (from model config or client headers), per-layer compatibility scoring (fast heuristics computed from kernel profiles), and recent observed quantization success rate. This avoids gratuitous fallbacks for requests that can run entirely in INT8.
- We did not implement model-rewrite to stitch different precision layers into a single fused kernel (out of scope for this PR). Instead we focus on runtime orchestration and cheap data-path transforms.
- The KVPrefetchAdapter supports three modes: exact-layout (prefetch using kernel's preferred layout), dequant-inline (prefetch with small dequant tokens appended), and universal (store in a neutral layout and convert on load). The adapter selects mode based on memory pressure and observed conversion cost.

Testing and results summary:
- microbench/perf/hetero_quant_bench reports: average latency unchanged, P99 improved by ~12% on a mixed INT8/FP8 workload compared to naive device-level fallback, and token throughput improved ~6% under 75% quantizable workload.
- CI runs: linux-build: pass; cuda-tests: initially flaky (race in coordinator startup), fixed and re-run: pass; lint: pass; benchmarks: included baseline.

Backwards compatibility: Coordinator integrates behind an opt-in runtime flag (--hetero-quant-fallback=on). Default behavior is unchanged unless the flag is enabled. KV adapter is gated behind a config flag and defaults to universal mode for older deployments.

Follow-ups:
- Expand kernel-side fast-paths to accept pre-converted KV layouts to further reduce dequant overhead.
- Add a sampling-based evaluator to surface which layers would most benefit from static model rewrites.

References: Linear ENG-7421 for the incident ticket and ENG-7523 for the follow-up performance work; SUP-1982 captured customer repro traces.

review_conversation: Ethan Morales (2026-02-22): Can you explain how the epoched precision-map avoids stale decisions when models are rolled out quickly? Suggest adding a TTL and metrics for decision staleness.
Priya Shah (2026-02-22): Added TTL and a precision.map.stale counter, and documented the tradeoffs (PR updated).
Wei Zhang (2026-02-24): I saw a small memory regression in the bench run. Is the staging buffer size configurable? We should bound it based on GPUs and model context length.
Priya Shah (2026-02-24): Made the staging buffer tunable via runtime config and added a safeguard to cap entries per-GPU. Bench results re-run and mem regression resolved.

Lucas Carter (2026-02-26): CI showed a sporadic crash on coordinator init under heavy concurrency. Looks like a startup race with the epoch counter. Please harden initialization and add a test that spawns many concurrent routers.
Priya Shah (2026-02-27): Fixed the race (commit g9d2a44), added the concurrent init test; CI green after rerun.
notes_on_benchmarks: P99 improved ~12% on mixed INT8/FP8 test harness; throughput +6% for 75% quantizable mix; microbench added to tests/perf/hetero_quant_bench.py
release_notes: Introduce opt-in heterogeneous quantization fallback coordinator and KV prefetch adapter to reduce tail latencies on mixed-precision fleets; enable via --hetero-quant-fallback flag.
additional_context: This PR targets runtime-level mitigation for mixed-precision kernel switching costs and KV layout mismatches. It is intentionally orthogonal to static model rewrites and quantization table changes.
